Introduction

Your son received an internship offer from a small gas company called Tokyo Gas Yamanashi.

Before he decides, you want to check the company properly.

The name sounds big, but this is not the main Tokyo Gas in the capital.

It is a smaller regional company in Yamanashi Prefecture.

In this lesson, you will learn simple English words to talk about parent companies and group companies. You will read short texts about Tokyo Gas and its group. You will practice questions you can ask the company.

Our goal is simple: help you research this offer calmly and ask good questions, so your son can make a smart choice.

Summary

You learned that a subsidiary, or kogaisha, is a smaller company owned by a parent company. But it keeps its own name, offices, and staff.

Tokyo Gas Co., Ltd., founded in 1885, is one of Japan's largest city gas companies and serves the Tokyo area.

Tokyo Gas Network manages the pipelines.

Tokyo Gas Yamanashi is the regional group company for Yamanashi Prefecture, handling both city gas and LPG propane.

To research the offer, write down the exact legal company name from the offer letter. Find the official website. Read the company overview (kaisha gaiyō). Check the parent company. Read the internship program details.

Prepare questions about the department, the daily work, and the mentor.

Remember: a famous name matters less than what your son will really see, learn, and practice during the internship.
